identification.description: A NOAA-maintained global collection of historical and near-real-time daily weather observations from land-based stations. It brings together observations from about 30 source networks and applies standard quality-control checks.
identification.citation: Menne, M. J., Durre, I., Korzeniewski, B., McNeill, S., Thomas, K., Yin, X., Anthony, S., Ray, R., Vose, R. S., Gleason, B. E., and Houston, T. G. (2012). Global Historical Climatology Network - Daily (GHCN-Daily), Version 3. [indicate subset used]. NOAA National Climatic Data Center. doi:10.7289/V5D21VHZ [access date].

leads.name: Matthew J. Menne

people.note: NOAA metadata does not name one current individual as project leader, so the Operations Team is listed as curator.

instruments.summary: Ground-based rain gauges and other station-based precipitation measurement systems

categories.name: Rain gauges
categories.role: Primary instrument category named in NOAA metadata

instruments.note: A compilation of many national and international networks, so no single instrument applies to all stations. The data are not homogenized for historical changes in instruments and observing practice; check station source networks and station metadata for instrument-level detail.

temporal.start_note: Official Version 3 metadata. The earliest observation in the archive is 1832-01-01 (precipitation, Parramatta, Australia).
temporal.update_frequency: Daily, with a full-dataset rebuild about each weekend
temporal.record_length: Less than 1 year to more than 175 years, depending on station
temporal.note: Daily values are not always measured over the same 24-hour period at every station; observation times and conventions differ between networks.

spatial.note: Station density varies: dense in North America, Europe and parts of Australia; sparse in Africa, Antarctica and parts of South America.

data_format.format: Station files with geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude)

status.label: Ongoing / actively updated
evidence: Receives daily observations from many national and international sources
Station records are updated as new observations arrive
The full dataset is rebuilt periodically, generally each weekend
Successive daily updates are archived with unique version numbers

versions.note: NCEI: not to be used except in rare cases
